name: Doh-Snam
instructions: 1. Finely chop the pork meat and fat into small pieces.
2. Heat a pan and sauté chopped onions, ginger, garlic, and green chilies until fragrant.
3. Add the pork pieces and cook until browned and the fat is rendered.
4. Season with salt and black pepper.
5. Gradually pour in the fresh pork blood while stirring continuously to prevent clumping.
6. Simmer on low heat until the blood thickens and coats the meat, ensuring it is thoroughly cooked.
description: Doh-Snam is a traditional delicacy of the Khasi community in Meghalaya. It is a blood-based pork dish often prepared during festivals or special occasions, reflecting the indigenous culinary practice of utilizing the entire animal. It is known for its intense, iron-rich flavor and deep, dark color.
